title: Upgrade path for cross-encoder families with multilingual regression harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a safe upgrade path for our cross-encoder reranker family to improve multilingual ranking quality while keeping latency and cost within SLOs. This ticket covers model selection criteria, automated regression checks across ~12 languages, benching on CPU/GPU/quantized variants, and an incremental rollout plan with automated fallback to current production models.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Selected cross-encoder variants (3 sizes) pass the multilingual regression harness with no quality regression >1% MRR on critical test suites
A2: Latency P95 for top-of-stack variant <= 1.4x current prod baseline for 512-token inputs on Dedicated GPUs
A3: End-to-end rerank throughput scales linearly with configured batch window up to 2k qps in our dedicated test cluster
A4: Canary rollout automation and alerting configured (Datadog + Slack) with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions
A5: Release notes, model cards, and cost delta estimate published in Confluence and shared with Solutions & Sales
tasks: T1: Assemble candidate cross-encoder family (compact/standard/large) with multilingual training checkpoints and docstrings
T2: Build multilingual regression harness (English + 11 other languages) and add to CI as nightly job
T3: Run latency/throughput matrix across hardware (A100, T4, CPU) and quantization options; capture KV cache behavior
T4: Iterate on kernel selection flags and batching window to meet latency targets
T5: Create canary runbook and add automated dashboard panels and SLO alerts
T6: Draft rollout communication and model card; schedule review with PM and Legal
evaluation_plan: Benchmarks: MRR@10, NDCG@5, Recall@100, latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU memory footprint
Datasets: internal multilingual evaluation sets (search/recommendation + paraphrase), MS MARCO translations, and customer-submitted holdouts
Per-language slices: en, es, fr, de, pt, nl, it, ja, ko, zh, ar, ru
Regression thresholds: per-slice MRR drop <= 1.0% or NDCG drop <= 0.8% vs prod baseline; otherwise fail
Automated CI: nightly run with artifacts stored in GCS and summarized to a metrics dashboard
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal staging validation with synthetic traffic (1 day)
Phase 1: 1% production traffic canary (48 hours) with live A/B evaluation against prod model
Phase 2: 10% traffic if no regressions for 72 hours
Phase 3: 30% -> 60% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers on MRR or latency SLO breach
Fallback: route to smaller quantized variant or previous prod model automatically when latency exceeds threshold or error rate spikes
notes_progress: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with research and infra. Identified three candidate checkpoints: xenc-compact-multi-v1, xenc-standard-multi-v2, xenc-large-multi-v1.
2025-02-18: Prototype harness implemented; initial English-only MRR shows +2.1% for standard variant but latency P95 is 1.8x baseline on T4.
2025-02-24: Kernel selection flags adjusted; continuous-batching window reduced from 50ms to 20ms to improve P95; observed modest throughput regression (-6%).
2025-02-28: Added per-language slices; Japanese and Arabic show >1.5% MRR regression on compact variant — holding compact out of immediate rollout.
2025-03-03: Datadog dashboards wired up (dashboards/g/abc123/rerank-upgrade) and initial canary runbook drafted. PR for CI harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/2345

2025-03-05: Decision: proceed with standard and large variants for staged rollout; compact will be revisited after further fine-tuning and data augmentation for low-resource languages. Planning release/runtime-1.20
review_feedback: PM (Lina Gomez): Confirm cost delta and contractual customer impact before 30% rollout.
Design (Marco Liu): Ensure model card includes per-language failure modes and guidance for embeddings pre-filtering.
Security (Priya Shah): No immediate KMS implications but coordinate if model artifacts contain PII from customer holdouts.
Infra (Owen K.): Request an additional benchmark on Dedicated autoscaling under mixed QPS bursts to verify tail latency behavior.
